Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The invention relates to an accessory device assembly for low or medium voltage electric applications. The accessory device includes a casing and electronic means including one or more current flowing in an electric cable. The top shell of the casing includes an external recess having a cable seat for accommodating the electric cable in a transversal position with respect to the casing. The cable seat has a cable coupling surface adapted to mechanically couple with the electrical cable. The accessory device comprises a holder element mechanically coupleable with the top shell in the external recess. The holder element includes one or more holding surfaces. Each of the holding surfaces is overlapped and mechanically coupled with the electric cable, when the holder element is positioned in the external recess in a corresponding accommodating position that is selectable depending on the size of the electric cable. Each of the holding surfaces, when overlapped and coupled with the electric cable, cooperates with the cable coupling surface to hold the electric cable in a given position with respect to the current sensors.

A top shell of the casing includes an external recess provided with a cable seat for accommodating the electric cable in a transverse position with respect to the casing. The cable seat has a cable coupling surface adapted to mechanically couple with the electric cable.

The invention concerns an accessory device assembly intended for low- or medium-voltage electrical uses. The accessory device has a casing and electronic components that include one or more current sensors configured to detect current flowing through an electric cable. A top shell of the casing is provided with an outer recess that includes a cable seat for receiving the electric cable in a position transverse to the casing. The cable seat has a cable-engaging surface designed to mechanically connect with the electric cable.

The accessory device also includes a holder element that can be mechanically joined to the top shell within the outer recess. This holder element has one or more retaining surfaces. When the holder element is placed in the outer recess in a respective receiving position selected according to the diameter or size of the electric cable, each retaining surface overlaps and mechanically engages the electric cable. In that engaged condition, each retaining surface works together with the cable-engaging surface to keep the electric cable in a predetermined position relative to the current sensors.

The invention relates to an accessory device assembly intended for use in low or medium voltage electrical applications.

The accessory device comprises a casing that houses electronic components configured to perform one or more monitoring, measuring, or control functions. Among these electronic components are current sensors arranged to measure the electric current flowing through an electric cable associated with the accessory device.

The casing includes a top shell provided with an external recess. This recess defines a cable seat shaped to receive and accommodate the electric cable. In particular, the cable seat is arranged so that the electric cable extends transversely with respect to the casing when positioned in the recess. The cable seat includes a cable coupling surface intended to contact or support the electric cable during operation.

The accessory device assembly further comprises a holder element configured to be mechanically coupled to the top shell of the casing within the external recess. The holder element can be positioned in different configurations according to the size, and in particular the diameter or cross-section, of the electric cable to be received in the cable seat.

When coupled to the top shell, the holder element cooperates with the cable coupling surface of the cable seat to retain the electric cable in a stable and fixed position. In this way, the electric cable is held at a predetermined location relative to the current sensors housed inside the casing. This stable positioning improves the accuracy and reliability of the current measurements performed by the accessory device, while also allowing the assembly to accommodate electric cables of different sizes.
outputs.L4:
An accessory device assembly for low or medium voltage electrical applications is provided for mounting on, or in association with, an electrical cable and for detecting or measuring current flowing through that cable. The assembly includes a casing that houses current-sensing electronics, such as one or more current sensors and associated processing or signal-conditioning components. The casing is shaped to define a recessed cable seat or cable-receiving region configured to receive a portion of an electrical cable. The cable seat includes a cable coupling surface against which the cable can be positioned during installation and use.

To allow the same accessory device assembly to be used with cables having different outside diameters, the assembly further includes a holder element that is movable or installable in a plurality of selectable positions relative to the casing. In each selectable position, the holder element defines a different effective cable-retaining space in cooperation with the recessed cable seat. The holder element includes one or more holding surfaces arranged to engage, support, or press against the cable. By selecting the appropriate position of the holder element, an installer can adapt the assembly to a particular cable size while maintaining the cable in a stable and repeatable position within the cable seat.

When the cable is received in the recessed seat, the holding surfaces of the holder element cooperate with the cable coupling surface of the casing to retain the cable transversely with respect to the casing. This cooperation limits unwanted movement of the cable, such as radial displacement, lateral shifting, or vibration, that could otherwise affect the accuracy of current sensing or compromise the mechanical integrity of the installation. The cable is therefore held in a predetermined position relative to the current-sensing electronics housed in the casing.

This arrangement improves both mechanical stability and sensing reliability. Mechanically, the holder element helps secure the cable without requiring a different accessory device for each cable diameter. Electrically and functionally, maintaining a consistent spatial relationship between the cable and the current sensors supports more accurate and repeatable current detection. The assembly is particularly suitable for use in switchgear, distribution equipment, protection devices, monitoring systems, and other low or medium voltage installations where compactness, ease of installation, and dependable current measurement are desired.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an accessory device assembly used in low or medium voltage electrical applications, including a casing, current sensors, a cable seat, and an adjustable holder element for different cable sizes.
counterfactuals.output: An accessory device assembly for low or medium voltage electrical applications is disclosed. The assembly includes a casing defining an internal compartment and at least one cable seat configured to receive an electrical cable. One or more current sensors are arranged in the casing relative to the cable seat to detect current flowing through the cable. A holder element is associated with the cable seat and is adjustable between different operating positions to accommodate cables of different diameters or cross-sectional sizes. The holder element is configured to retain the cable in a predetermined position with respect to the current sensors, thereby promoting reliable current measurement while enabling use of the assembly with a range of cable sizes. The casing may further provide mechanical protection and positioning support for the current sensors, the cable seat, and the adjustable holder element.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following invention in formal patent language: a casing with a top shell recess receives an electric cable transversely, and a removable holder has multiple selectable holding surfaces to secure cables of different diameters relative to current sensors.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus comprises a casing defining a recess in a top shell thereof, the recess being configured to receive an electric cable extending transversely with respect to the casing. A removable holder is selectively mountable in the recess and includes a plurality of selectable cable-holding surfaces. Each holding surface is configured to engage and retain a respective electric cable diameter so as to position the electric cable in a predetermined relationship relative to one or more current sensors disposed in the casing. The holder is replaceable or reorientable to accommodate cables of different diameters while maintaining alignment between the cable and the current sensors.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical description of an electrical accessory device that mechanically holds an electric cable in a recess of its casing so the cable remains positioned with respect to internal current sensing electronics.
counterfactuals.output:
An electrical accessory device includes a casing, current sensing electronics housed within the casing, and a cable-retention arrangement configured to mechanically hold an electric cable in a predetermined position relative to the current sensing electronics.

The casing defines a cable-receiving recess extending along an outer or internal surface of the casing. The recess is dimensioned to receive at least a portion of an insulated electric cable and to guide the cable along a defined path adjacent to a sensing region of the device. The sensing region may include, for example, a current transformer, Hall-effect sensor, magnetoresistive sensor, Rogowski coil, or other current sensing element arranged to detect current flowing through the cable when the cable is positioned in the recess.

A mechanical holding member is associated with the recess to retain the cable therein. The holding member may comprise one or more resilient clips, snap-fit arms, clamping ribs, retaining tabs, hinged covers, over-center latches, or deformable gripping projections formed integrally with or attached to the casing. The holding member applies a retaining force to the cable sufficient to prevent accidental displacement of the cable from the recess during installation, handling, or operation, while maintaining the cable in a substantially fixed spatial relationship with the current sensing electronics.

In one configuration, the recess has a generally channel-shaped profile with side walls and a base surface, and the retaining member spans at least part of the recess opening to prevent the cable from lifting out of the channel. The retaining member may be elastically deflectable so that the cable can be pressed into the recess during assembly and thereafter held by a snap engagement. Alternatively, a movable clamp or cover may be closed over the cable after placement in the recess.

By mechanically locating the cable in the recess, the device maintains a repeatable distance, orientation, and alignment between the conductor and the sensing element. This improves measurement consistency and reduces sensitivity to cable movement, vibration, or installation variation. The retention arrangement also allows the current sensing electronics to be calibrated or configured based on a known cable position within the casing.

The casing may further include guide surfaces, stops, or locating features that define the insertion depth and lateral position of the cable. The recess and retaining member may be sized to accommodate one or more predetermined cable diameters, or may include compliant features to accommodate a range of cable sizes while preserving the required positional relationship with the sensing electronics.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an invention disclosure paragraph for a low/medium voltage device assembly where a cable is seated in an external recess and clamped by a holder element having several alternative cable-contacting surfaces.
counterfactuals.output: A low/medium voltage device assembly is disclosed comprising a housing or support body having an externally accessible recess configured to receive and seat an electrical cable, and a holder element mountable to the housing to retain the cable in the recess. The recess may be formed on an outer surface of the device assembly so that the cable can be positioned without opening an internal compartment of the device. The holder element includes a plurality of alternative cable-contacting surfaces, each surface being selectively positionable toward the recess to accommodate cables of different diameters, shapes, insulation thicknesses, or stiffnesses. In one embodiment, the holder element is reversible, rotatable, indexable, or otherwise re-orientable so that a selected one of the cable-contacting surfaces cooperates with the recess to define a cable clamping passage. The cable-contacting surfaces may have different radii, profiles, depths, textures, or resilient features to provide controlled retention while reducing risk of damage to the cable insulation. A fastening arrangement, such as one or more screws, clips, latches, or snap-fit features, secures the holder element to the housing and urges the selected cable-contacting surface against the seated cable. The assembly thereby provides an external, adaptable cable retention arrangement suitable for low or medium voltage devices, enabling simplified installation, strain relief, and reliable positioning of different cable types using a common holder element.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.output: An accessory device comprising: a casing; electronic current-sensing means disposed in or supported by the casing; a cable coupling surface configured to receive a portion of an electrical cable in operative proximity to the electronic current-sensing means; and a holder element associated with the casing and selectable between a plurality of accommodating positions, wherein each accommodating position is configured to retain a different cable size against or adjacent the cable coupling surface for current sensing by the electronic current-sensing means.
